Definition: from G4059; circumcision (the rite, the condition or the people, literally or figuratively):--X circumcised, circumcision.
BiblicalUsage: Peritome is circumcision, the sign God gave Abraham, and in the New Testament it stands for the whole question of who belongs to God. Paul says the true Jew is not the one outwardly circumcised but the one circumcised in heart, by the Spirit. In Christ, he says, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, and believers have received a circumcision made without hands, the putting off of the body of the flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe circumcision teaches me that God's mark was never on the flesh first; it was always on the heart. The rite pointed forward to a cutting away of the old nature, and Christ has done that cutting for everyone who trusts Him. So I hold that no outward sign can make me God's, and no lack of one can keep me from Him.
